claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions.

Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children you're responsible for, and if so, how many?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I have one child - my son Alex. He's 17 and lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. To assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to ask you a few more questions.

Since Alex is 17, his eligibility depends on whether he's in approved education or training. **Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** (For example, is he studying at school, college, or doing an approved training course?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in school or college at the moment. He finished his GCSEs last year but hasn't gone on to do A-levels or anything like that.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I need to understand Alex's current situation a bit more.

**Is Alex currently working? If so, how many hours per week does he work?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not working at the moment. He's just been at home trying to figure out what he wants to do next.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying. I have a few more questions to complete the assessment.

**Has Alex registered with a government-sponsored careers service or with the armed services?** (This would allow Child Benefit to continue for up to 20 weeks after leaving education or training.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not sure actually - I don't know if he's done that or not.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's okay. Let me ask a follow-up question to help determine the timeline:

**When did Alex leave education or training? Was it within the last 20 weeks, or was it longer ago than that?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He left school over a year ago now, so it's definitely been longer than 20 weeks.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. I have one more important question:

**Is Alex currently claiming any benefits in his own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not claiming any benefits himself.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. Let me also ask about your own circumstances:

**Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, I'm afraid **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why:

- You normally qualify for Child Benefit for children under 16, or for those aged 16-19 if they stay in **approved education or training**
- Alex is 17, so he's over 16, which means his eligibility depends on whether he's in approved education or training
- Alex left school over a year ago and is not currently in any approved education or training
- There is a provision that allows Child Benefit to continue for up to 20 weeks after a 16 or 17 year old leaves education, if they register with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services - but Alex left education over a year ago, so this extension period has passed

**What you might consider:** If Alex decides to return to education or approved training in the future, you could potentially claim Child Benefit again at that point. You would need to make a new claim if his circumstances change.

I hope this clarifies your situation. If Alex's circumstances do change, please feel free to reach out again.
